newsitem.title: INDIA: OPINION - WEEKLY TECHNICAL ANALYSIS OF BSE/NSE SHARE INDEXES.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - WEEKLY TECHNICAL ANALYSIS OF BSE/NSE SHARE INDEXES.

text.p: BULL TREND LIKELY TO FACE RESISTANCE is a trend
analysis of the National Stock Exchange and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) indexes for the period December 31 to January 3 by analyst Mehmood Khan at Times Guaranty Financials Ltd

Thursday's trading saw the Nifty rise by 25.45 points (2.88 percent) at 910.65 level over the previous day. With this the index has conclusively cleared the 61.8 percent retracement of the decline (3344.67 - 2713.12). This and the speed of the current rally indicate that the current bullish trend is healthy, and therefore, the lowest point of the rise formed at 2713.12 is likely to offer good support in case the index declines towards that level.

On the upside the rally is likely to face resistance at the 3168-3218 levels. This is mainly because the index is taking more time in reaching this important pivot than it took to reach the lowest point at 2713.12. The weakness is reconfirmed by the speed of the rise @ 29.58 points per trading day as compared to the speed of the previous decline from 3035.64 to 2713.12 at the rate of 46.07 points per trading day. Hence one should be prepared for the corrective decline.

The mechanical oscillators on the monthly bar charts, of Andhra Valley, Apollo Tyres, Arvind Mills, Ashok Leyland, BSES, Bajaj Auto BHEL, Colgate, Glaxo, HDFC, Indo-gulf fertilizers, Escorts, L&T, OBC, SBI & Tata Chem depicts that these stocks would be very volatile exhibiting potential buying interest on declining volumes. The bullish phenomia would sustain at best in these stocks till January 8, 1997. By the close of the month these stocks would experience a substantial erosion in their value and may probably close lower than the December 1996 close.

The interim rally from 2713.12, has retraced the decline of a larger degree from 3344.67 by 61.80 percent (3103.42). The Sensex may encounter resistance at the left & right shoulders (3176) levels. The rally may lose momentum at the 67 percent to 80 percent (i.e. 3134 - 3218). The mechanical oscillators in conjunction with the volume justify that the top may be formed at (3167.83 - 3193.10). The trend following indicators justify that the rally will lose momentum at the 200-week average at 3196.11.

The price following oscillators on the weekly bar chart are exhibiting that the top may be formed at 3168-3218 levels - Relative Strength Index (14 RSI) is 44.20, Price Rate of Change (12 ROC) is placed at -0.52, short term stochastic is hovering at 69.88 and its trigger line is at 52.13, while the medium term stochastic is 30.82 and the trigger is 25.16, the Macd is -133.12 and its trigger is -126.22 & the 14 William's percent R is placed at -43.66.

For the current week, the BSE Sensex in the upmove may encounter resistance at 3167, 3193 & 3218 levels, on the lower end it may find support at 3065-3042 levels. The National Index may witness profit booking at 1385-1411 levels and support at 1354 & 1336 levels.
(The opinions expressed in this article reflect the views of the author only. They should not be taken as reflecting the views of Reuters).
